Description:
The Carbon 9 Defense - Compliance App extends federal logging compliance coverage for OMB Memorandum M-26-14, which governs effective and efficient agency logging and network visibility to defend against evolving cyber threats. The app provides compliance dashboards, maturity model assessments, and Threat Hunting and Incident Response Framework (THIRF) objective tracking aligned to M-26-14 requirements. It operates as a soft companion to Compliance Essentials for Splunk, sharing compatible data structures but requiring no hard dependency. The app uses three KV store collections to track systems inventory, manual attestation scores, and configuration parameters, alongside two CSV lookups that map systems to expected sourcetypes and event hosts to system identifiers. Four saved searches compute Inventory Visibility, Collection Coverage, Asset Snapshots, and merged Maturity Scores, enabling automated tracking of compliance posture over time. The app is intended for Compliance Officers managing federal logging posture, SOC Analysts tracking event log coverage and retention, and Federal IT administrators implementing M-26-14 controls.

item.title: Log10x App - v1.1.4 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
\- The app's searchable copy of each template is now written with Splunk's \`collect\` as sourcetype \`stash\`, which Splunk does not count against the licence. Template records sent by the Receiver are counted as before. \- Two different templates under one template hash are detected when stored. Their events stay compact and carry \`tenx\_expand\_refused\=hash-conflict\` instead of expanding with the wrong text, and the Diagnostics dashboard lists them. \- A stored template that is a cut-short copy of the one the Receiver sends is replaced by the whole template. \- A compact event from a template with no values now expands. \- The new \`tx\` command takes the search as written, with no \`searchstring\=\` option and no escaped quotes: \`| tx index\=app\_logs sourcetype\=tenx\_encoded "payment failed" NOT retry\`. \`tenxsearch\` works as before. \- Recompile all managed alerts keeps the rest of an alert's pipeline, such as \`| stats count\`, when it converts a \`tenxsearch\` alert, and converts \`tx\` alerts too.


Short Description:
Send Splunk the logs that sampling and filters keep out to fit the license, on that same license. Compact events take a fraction of the volume and expand back byte-identical at search time; classic dashboards keep their SPL, and one command covers the search bar, saved searches, alerts and the REST API.


Description:
With the Log10x App, Splunk can index compact log events and still search, chart and alert on the original lines. The 10x Receiver stores each event as a template hash plus the values that change, so a stream of repeated patterns takes less of the license. On the OpenTelemetry demo the bytes sent to Splunk shrank by 63.7%, encoded events and template dictionary counted together, and every line expanded back byte-identical with the Receiver settings in the installation steps (measurement: https://www.log10x.com/blog/cutting-splunk-log-storage/). The same license then holds more: sources that were sampled, filtered or kept out of Splunk to stay under the limit can come back, or the license can be smaller. Classic dashboards keep their SPL: the browser sends each panel's search to the app, which rewrites it on the server. From the search bar, saved searches, alerts and the REST API, a search is wrapped in the tenxsearch command. An alert created in the app's Compile Alert view is compiled once into a native saved search, so the scheduler runs no Python. NOT, OR, groups, phrases, field conditions, and values such as IP addresses and hostnames behave as they do on the original data. The 10x Receiver produces compact events, and it is free on up to 10 nodes (https://www.log10x.com/pricing). No sign-up is required to evaluate it: with no license token it runs the full product for 30 days on up to 10 nodes, air-gapped, and a free license removes the time limit (https://doc.log10x.com/manage/license/). The app itself is open source under the MIT license.

item.title: Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on for Splunk - v4.0.50 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Important for upgrades: [Review the legacy dynamic-sourcetype upgrade checks](http://sh-i-ak:8003/en-US/app/TA_cisco_catalyst/user_guide#upgrade-checks-for-legacy-dynamic-sourcetypes) before migrating saved searches or alerts. * **NetFlow setup alignment:** Made setup step boxes equal in height and aligned package installation status and version rows at the bottom of each card. The layout continues to wrap on narrower screens. * **Open-page upgrade detection:** Setup, input editors and Data Collection Health check for updated UI assets and offer **Reload updated add-on**. Save or discard unsaved edits first; each open tab reloads separately. Existing pages opened before this feature was installed still need one hard refresh (Chrome/Edge: Mac Command + Shift + R; Windows Ctrl + Shift + R). * **NetFlow receiver guidance:** Separated SD-WAN Manager instructions, the saved-port/action row and unsaved-port explanation so they wrap without overlapping. Saving behavior and listener settings are unchanged. * **Configuration organization:** Grouped packaged configuration and input specifications by product under consistent headings, with separate shared, network syslog and NetFlow sections. Build output preserves the organization; stanza names and setting values are unchanged. * **HF configuration:** Resource Utilization compares merged collector settings against the tuning table, flags throughput caps and baseline differences, and identifies stale/unavailable evidence and Cloud-managed exceptions. * **Controller request pressure:** Application catalog reads share conservative pacing. SD-WAN device tasks reuse bounded, thread-local connections and report unsupported/disconnected counts separately. Exact CG522-E DRE capability responses use expiring skips. * **ISE KV recovery:** Initialization responses receive a shared 60-second retry budget; persistent failures remain errors. Data Quality includes ISE KV failures. Use canonical `cisco:ise:syslog`. * **Documentation accuracy and logging choice:** Clarified the TA's HSL production default separately from Cisco's selective SUL troubleshooting guidance, linked the vendor restrictions, and distinguished pass/drop/inspect support from complete or continuous coverage. Reconciled current input counts, sourcetype references, CSV/JSON report support, companion package identity, dependency versions and acceleration sizing. Existing data, input defaults and historical release entries are preserved. * **Issue recovery after prolonged failures:** An unfinished Issue window whose end is more than 48 hours old moves to one verified historical checkpoint without discarding its saved progress. Historical and current collection alternate one lane per scheduled poll. Both retain the existing request rate, output ordering and limits. Poll logs identify the lane, pending windows and actual failed window/offset; vendor HTTP 5xx and exhausted 429 responses are distinguished from internal errors. A completed lane remains `recovering` while another window is pending. This prevents old-window starvation; it does not resolve upstream HTTP 504s or guarantee historical backfill. * **SD-WAN audit checkpoint recovery:** Bounded adaptive audit windows to 24 hours and sanitized retained tuning values before checkpoint writes. Sparse polling can no longer grow an integer beyond Python JSON serialization limits. Existing completed timestamps and boundary identities are preserved; deployment and worker activation are required for affected inputs to recover. Previously replayed events are not removed. * **Direct resource telemetry:** Data Collection Health CPU and memory charts use indexed `_introspection` process fields through `tstats`, with host/product filters and no data model acceleration. The retired TA resource model is no longer packaged. * **C2C reporting setup reference:** Added a direct App Setup link to the C2C installation guide, with environment-specific configuration, location mapping and v4.0.20 compatibility notes. Clarified that the current master reporting search already removes the sort result cap; large-inventory completeness and performance still require validation. * **ISE analytics eventtype availability:** The TA enables its six ISE analytics eventtypes under its existing app-wide system sharing. FullReport, Hardware, and Registry searches retain the same current-and-historical predicates; the companion App continues to own the data model. Install the TA on the search head as well as the collector; customer local overrides remain authoritative and require separate review if an eventtype is unavailable. * **Device Health sourcetype display:** Removed the interface enablement note from Device Health rows without legacy interface collection enabled. Interface sourcetype help now points to the standalone Interface Statistics input and explains the upgrade compatibility path. Existing legacy settings and collection behavior are unchanged. * **Device Health site discovery:** Handles controllers that omit the hierarchy path on the Global root, so that root no longer prevents the site picker and scoped collection from loading valid child sites. Global remains browse-only; missing paths on ordinary sites still stop discovery. * **Dependency security:** Updated Moment to 2.31.0, brace-expansion to 1.1.21, fast-uri to 3.1.8 and webpack-dev-middleware to 7.4.6 for reported advisories. These include development-tool dependencies as well as the frontend Moment dependency. * **Security Advisory completeness:** Older Catalyst Center APIs can report complete collection when advisory counts, device relationships and repeated advisory metadata reconcile. Missing evidence, hidden devices or changes during collection keep the input in a recovering state. * **Security Advisory collection limits:** Modern advisory reads share a conservative 100-request-per-minute allowance across advisory IDs, keeping pacing state bounded for large catalogs. An advertised snapshot above 100,000 advisory/device pairs or with invalid counts fails before relationship collection; supported snapshots still reconcile every relationship, including zero-count results. * **Fewer Security Advisory requests:** On modern controllers, collection uses the per-device advisory API when its worst-case page count is lower than the per-advisory walk. Every advisory still reconciles against its advertised affected-device count before output. An unavailable first device request falls back to the existing path; later failures remain incomplete. Legacy controllers retain their existing collection path. * **Report format visibility:** The scheduled-report selector shows CSV/JSON formats and identifies unsupported formats such as Tableau Data Extract before collection. Existing report selections and automatic selection remain unchanged. * **Bounded report downloads:** Scheduled CSV/JSON exports are limited to 32 MiB of decompressed data and 250,000 records per report. Oversized, partial or interrupted downloads fail that selection without publishing its records; other selected reports can continue. Filter or split larger exports in Catalyst Center. CSV parsing avoids retaining multiple full row lists, while preserving BOMs, separator directives, quoted multiline values and existing field names. * **Report parsing memory:** JSON resource checks run before object allocation, including nested and unused metadata. Each document is limited to 128 nesting levels, 500,002 objects/arrays and 4,000,000 values; exceeding a limit fails the report. CSV downloads are parsed from bounded bytes without a full decoded-text/re-encoding round trip. Standard JSON validation and existing report fields are preserved. * **ISE API diagnostics:** Failed HTTP requests retain a bounded, credential-redacted controller response in the internal logs, with the endpoint, status and final attempt. Successful response bodies are not logged, and retries and collection limits are unchanged. * **Data Quality:** Checkpoint error detection includes collection tracebacks and preserves full input names, so failed KV Store writes are not reported as a clean window. * **Flexible health time ranges:** The dashboard and Data Quality time controls now use the standard Splunk time picker. Choose presets, relative ranges, dates, exact start/end times or advanced historical ranges. New dashboard sessions match the native Last 4 hours preset (`-4h@m` to `now`); shared links preserve their exact bounds and use the Splunk user's timezone. * **Interface Statistics enablement:** Corrected the saved-account configuration lookup used when enabling or re-enabling standalone collection. Ownership checks use one account snapshot, and disabling an established owner keeps legacy Device Health interface collection paused to prevent unexpected or duplicate collection. ##### Authentication and input clarity * **Connection-test isolation:** Persistent handlers use an add-on-specific process configuration so other apps cannot replace their imported modules or library paths. Startup failures record module-path evidence. ISE Data Connect distinguishes missing driver imports from operating-system, TLS and network errors, without logging credential values. * **Collection diagnostics:** Health cards distinguish recent data from complete collection. Select **inputs need attention** to see affected inputs, collectors, latest reasons and poll times. ISE's full product name is recognized; API call-volume tables preserve full input identity and separate collectors. Catalyst Center tests avoid loading the account-save framework and return readable startup errors. Shared ISE runtime summaries retain separate resource failures instead of showing only the first permission error. Product summaries keep the displayed sourcetype, age and expected interval together. Syslog canaries handle healthy and empty results without a false incomplete-results warning. * **SD-WAN authentication:** Rejects HTML, redirects and malformed XSRF token responses before constructing request headers. Collection retries once with a fresh session, then reports authentication failure without logging tokens or response bodies. * **Connection tests:** Report whether TLS certificate verification passed, was disabled, or was not performed for an HTTP connection. Authentication success no longer implies certificate verification ran. * **Application Inventory:** Renamed the Catalyst Center application catalog input from Application Traffic. Saved input identifiers and settings are preserved. New output now uses `cisco:dnac:application:inventory`; the transition eventtype includes retained `cisco:dnac:application:traffic` history. **Upgrade action:** Delete the existing Application Traffic / Application Inventory input and create a new **Application Inventory** input with the corrected sourcetype, preserving account, index, interval and log level. Creation and editing forms explain the sourcetype change and compatibility behavior. It collects catalog metadata, not interval byte or packet counters. * **SD-WAN response clarity:** Certificate-chain reads are Advanced and point to the certificate statistics endpoints for periodic health monitoring. Non-JSON responses remain failures with safe response-shape diagnostics. Real-Time poll counts distinguish successful targeted devices from all devices observed in bulk responses, preserving collected records. * **Bundled SSH libraries:** Updated cryptography to 50.0.1, PyNaCl to 1.6.2, cffi to 2.0.0 and Paramiko to 5.0.0 for Linux/Windows Python 3.9, 3.11 and 3.13; added its Invoke dependency. Paramiko 5 removes DSA, SHA-1 RSA signatures, SHA-1 key exchange and GSSAPI. Validate modern SSH algorithms and ISE report SSH/SFTP before upgrading. * **HTTP security and compatibility:** Upgraded urllib3 to 2.8.0 and fast-uri to 3.1.8. Version 4.0.50 supports Splunk Enterprise 9.4.0 or later, including Python 3.9 collectors, with the packaged Cisco compatibility backport; Python 3.13 remains preferred on Splunk 10.2+. A checksum-verified local UCC metadata patch permits the fixed HTTP library while preserving upstream UCC Python code; security scans continue checking its upstream advisories. * **Legacy HF recovery and input-list errors:** Builds containing the checksum-verified Python 3.9 compatibility backport retain urllib3 2.8.0 security fixes while correcting its runtime union alias, OpenSSL flag import and the Splunk Python 3.9/OpenSSL 1.0.2 TLS path. Certificate trust, TLS 1.2 minimum and SAN hostname validation remain enforced. The customer HF recovery build requires activation and fresh collection verification; upstream dependency Python support metadata is unchanged. Application Setup now reports failed input-list requests instead of presenting them as an empty configuration. Builds declare Python 3.9 and 3.13 and validate runtime selectors across every product. * **Site Health readiness:** Accepts one controller-recommended rewind of up to ten minutes for Site Health. Explicit time windows and fixed pagination boundaries remain protected, and diagnostics report the actual adjustment. * **ISE report memory:** Streams CSV conversion through a private temporary file and verifies transfer completion before ingestion. Memory is bounded by individual records instead of the full report; event fields and sourcetypes are preserved. Each CSV/JSON spool is limited to 512 MiB, one million rows and 2 MiB per JSON record; transfer failure or a limit breach stops that report before ingestion. Allow temporary disk space for concurrent reports. * **Legacy library cleanup:** Removed unused standalone Underscore 1.6.0 and companion jQuery files, and excluded obsolete framework bundles containing older Lodash and DOMPurify. Packages retain the assets emitted by the supported application pages, verified against build hashes. Confirm obsolete assets are removed when upgrading through Splunk Web or a remote installation that may retain old files. ##### Optional Device Health site scope * **Hierarchy accuracy and search:** Search results retain their ancestors and distinguish area, building and floor icons. A warning appears at 160 included sites so operators can plan for growth before the 200-site collection limit. Enrichment follows explicit node types and geographic metadata at every depth; business labels are no longer guessed to be countries, states, cities or campuses. Previously inferred fields can therefore be absent on new events. Existing event values and indexed history are preserved. * **Container membership completeness:** Fixed a parent-selection case that could silently miss devices in child sites. Some controllers return direct assignments for both the parent count and membership list; agreement between those responses does not prove descendant coverage. The collector now checks every included site before and after collection, deduplicates devices, and stops output when membership changes or a page fails. API savings require a measured pilot. * **Device scope** now offers **All managed devices** (unchanged default) or **Selected sites and descendants**. The selector loads site metadata only. Selecting a site includes child sites and newly assigned devices on subsequent polls. * Scoped collection sends site filters to the health API, retrieves site membership independently, and enriches only those device IDs in bounded batches. Inventory-only devices remain in the output. Membership is rechecked before writing events; incomplete or unsupported scope requests never fall back to controller-wide collection. * The existing sourcetype, device fields and timestamps remain unchanged. Scoped events add `collection_scope=sites` and `collection_site_ids`; poll diagnostics add scope, membership, request/byte and completeness evidence. Counts describe the chosen scope, not the whole controller. Data Collection Health provides scope-failure guidance. API compatibility and representative p95 duration still require a pilot; this is not a guarantee that API timeouts or limits are resolved. ##### Browser refresh after upgrades * The upgrade reminder appears only on the **Application Setup** landing page, keeping account/settings/input pages, Data Collection Health, and the User Guide free of repeated banners. It still instructs operators to hard-refresh each page or tab they use after every upgrade; refreshing only Application Setup does not refresh other open pages or editors. Finish or discard unsaved edits first. * The reminder uses smaller text and a single wrapping paragraph. Detailed instructions remain in the required upgrade actions and post-upgrade checklist. ##### Interface Statistics setup and inventory * Setup now loads account inventory before saving, with total devices, type/site counts, names, management IPs, models, status and refresh information. Unknown or incomplete data stays explicit. * Selected devices supports name/IP/model search, site/type filters, selection of all matches across pages and individual exceptions. The saved selection contains exact devices. * **Devices matching rules** adds automatic selection by type, site, name, model or IP, with All/Any conditions, exclusions and bounded regex patterns. Conditions are evaluated each poll so new matches are included. Missing fields remain explicit; existing All/Selected inputs retain their approval and behavior. * Inventory is visible initially, shows its update time, and offers **Retry loading** during a pending request. A separate timeout on the existing-collection check prevents it from keeping retries unavailable. * Interface Statistics uses the standard account/name/interval/index form and Create/Update flow. Advanced holds collection safeguards. Creating or enabling it automatically takes over interface collection; Device Health shades its old controls, names the managing input and links to it. Fixed handler startup and native save/enable requests. * Fixed the "Account and index are required" rejection during activation: partial Splunk updates are validated against the saved input, preserving account, index, scope and limits. * New Device Health inputs and existing inputs with interface collection off use the standalone Interface Statistics input. Reopening Device Health no longer exposes a legacy enable option. Saves can retain already-enabled legacy collection; after turning it off and saving, use Interface Statistics to collect interfaces again. * Upgrades preserve legacy settings and collection until a standalone input is created or enabled; no input is created automatically by the upgrade. Pausing the standalone input keeps interface collection paused. Deleting it can resume saved legacy collection. Site enrichment and `cisco:dnac:devicehealth:interface` remain unchanged. See [the upgrade procedure](http://sh-i-ak:8003/en-US/app/TA_cisco_catalyst/user_guide#upgrade-from-device-health-interface-collection). ##### Data Collection Health dashboard * **Collector evidence and tab guidance:** Added an HF / collector selector for internal-log, runtime/API and collector resource evidence, with shareable selection and explicit discovery failures. Product-data freshness and local configuration retain their independent scope. Every tab explains its Purpose, Expected behavior and Scope; PDF exports include that guidance. * **Retired Studio copy:** Removed the obsolete Dashboard Studio health view from the package. Data Collection Health continues to use the React dashboard through the existing navigation entry. Local shell builds/deployments clean up the retired packaged view; any separately saved user copies remain independently managed. * **Lookup coverage:** Fixed the invalid lookup match limit and made the shared health search use its named lookup definition. Standalone Interface Statistics now participates in expected-data checks with its 15-minute cadence recommendation; legacy Device Health interface collection retains its existing selector. Automated checks keep shipped lookup definitions, search references and collector mappings aligned. * **Consistent sections across tabs:** Current collection problems, freshness, ISE report-pipeline warnings, resource health and data-quality issues stay visible. Optional diagnostics use expandable sections with remembered state while switching tabs, **Expand all / Collapse all**, and direct section links. Closed headers distinguish unchecked, incomplete and unavailable evidence from known findings. The short Syslog Onboarding view remains fully visible; PDF preparation still includes every panel. * **Clearer Overview:** Equal-size responsive product cards distinguish indexed-data freshness from collector problems. **Needs attention** appears before activity charts; historical logs, coverage, collector versions, and duplicate checks are available in expandable sections. * **Focused evidence:** Diagnostic tables show essential columns first, with **Details** for the remaining fields. Empty results use compact messages; unavailable or incomplete evidence remains explicit. PDF export retains all tabs and diagnostic panels. * **More efficient searches:** Product cards share compatible freshness and collector searches. Closed diagnostic sections do not dispatch searches, unrelated filters no longer refresh every panel, and up to four dashboard jobs run at once. Abandoned jobs are cancelled, and preview limits remain visible. Search-performance improvements require representative production validation. ##### Collection support bundles * Fixed support exports hitting Splunk's event-preview storage limit by using a search mode that saves the complete bounded result set. Separate preview flags no longer reject complete results. Removed a wildcard warning that prevented available input settings from being included; completed counts and every exported page remain checked. * **Download support bundle** in Data Collection Health creates a ZIP of the selected products' searchable internal logs, available input settings, observed software versions and poll outcomes. It defaults to detected products and the last 24 hours; a diagnostic dialog can preselect its product. * Export preserves all recorded severities, repeated events and multiline traces. Pagination is reconciled against completed search counts; search warnings, truncation and required-search failures stop generation. Completed exports say **Bundle ready**, with missing optional context and products with no matching logs shown as separate warnings. The archive retains its coverage details. * Export-time secret redaction, a 50 MiB compressed maximum, a 200 MiB processing limit, a one-million-event ceiling and a five-minute deadline bound the operation. Files download locally for the customer to share; collection settings and log levels are unchanged. ##### Authentication and controller context * **SD-WAN session cookies:** Authentication extracts `JSESSIONID` by name from multi-cookie responses, including AWS WAF responses where `AWSALB` or `AWSALBCORS` precede it. * **Monitored software versions:** Internal logs identify the remote controller release separately from the TA release. Data Collection Health adds version tables on Overview and the four API product tabs, with source, check time, age, and explicit unknown/stale evidence. Dedicated inputs share bounded cached discovery; unavailable version evidence does not mark collection unhealthy. The dashboard grid also keeps full-width tables usable in narrower windows. * **Catalyst Center permissions:** Clarified 3.1.x versus 2.3.7.x API, Reports, and Audit Log permission names; added custom-role and Global access-group setup, with authentication and dataset access verified separately. ##### Catalyst Center and ISE collection health repairs * **Chart tooltips:** Long labels wrap cleanly; values remain visible. * **ISE snapshot timestamps:** ERS, Monitoring REST, pxGrid, Data Connect, Endpoint & Context, Guest, Threat, and Vulnerability snapshots explicitly set `_time` from `ise_observed_time`, the real output-time epoch, and retain `collection_time` as the snapshot key. Output is paced only above 50,000 events per second per input stream to reduce concentration at one timestamp. This is not fleet-scale qualification. Original vendor date fields remain unchanged. This prevents timezone-less dates inside a row from moving fresh snapshots into the future. The change applies to newly indexed events only; retained events are not retimed. Each JSON event has a 9,999,999-byte ceiling; an oversized event fails the output operation instead of being silently truncated, and the poll remains incomplete. * **Truthful health summaries:** Recovering inputs now appear in Current Collection Problems. Product tables no longer append an OK row beside partial or failed inputs. API Impact accepts canonical `event=api-call` telemetry, and configured-dataset detection reads complete comma-separated selections instead of only their first value. The current problem reason is taken from the latest poll on each collector host, so an older error cannot overwrite a newer completeness warning. Freshness remains separate from collection completeness. * **Upgrade cache handling:** Setup, input forms, and Data Collection Health load bundles using their packaged content versions during ordinary navigation. An explicit `_ta_build` page parameter remains available for troubleshooting. Open configuration and DCH pages check the installed asset manifest every five minutes while visible and on return/navigation (at most once per 30 seconds). A confirmed UI change displays a reload notice; failed checks do not prove an upgrade. Reload is always user-controlled. * **Expected diagnostics:** Unsupported selected reports keep `UnsupportedReportFormat` and a partial poll without an unhandled-exception traceback. ISE Open API version-route HTTP 404/405/501 responses are informational compatibility probes when the Monitoring fallback is attempted; authentication errors and failed fallback requests remain errors. * **Build dependency security:** Updated the UI build dependency `js-yaml` to 4.3.2 for [GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh). * **Analytics export retries:** The legacy individual-export fallback counts timed-out attempts as well as busy responses and stops after three tries. Existing export-completion checks and wait intervals remain; a long export wait is not by itself evidence of missing data. * **Client page sizing:** An explicit HTTP 400 maximum-limit response, including “Parameter limit has an invalid value… Value must be in the range 1-100,” can select one smaller server-advertised page size before the legacy 20-row fallback. Ambiguous errors still fail closed; count, ordering, deadline, and byte guards remain. For 73,533 clients, a supported 100-row page needs about 736 data calls versus 3,677 at 20, plus initial negotiation and any short-page continuation. This is arithmetic, not a capacity qualification. * **Customized scheduled reports:** CSV inventory and compliance reports require **Device Name** and **IP Address** to locate the header; **Device Type** is optional. UTF-8 BOM, separator directives, and quoted multiline values are supported. Existing report sourcetypes and field normalization are preserved. * **Report format selection:** Use CSV or JSON report executions. TDE, Hyper, ZIP, and PDF are not supported; binary signatures take precedence over misleading CSV filenames. A selected unsupported report remains a failed selection, with `UnsupportedReportFormat` in poll diagnostics. Recreate that report in CSV/JSON or remove it from the input selection. If **Collect all reports** is enabled, turn it off and select only supported reports. Other selected reports continue collecting. * **pxGrid credentials and health:** The pxGrid client password or certificate is separate from ERS credentials. Missing credentials, pending/disabled clients, HTTP failures, invalid responses, and absence of a successful service provider no longer appear as healthy empty Administrative polls. A valid empty bindings response still succeeds. Approve pending clients in ISE; periodic collection no longer performs approval. Verify that the configured client name and password/certificate match the approved ISE client. Do not reset or recreate the client merely to clear a health warning. * **ISE ERS compatibility:** The [Endpoint Certificate API](https://ciscoisesdk.readthedocs.io/en/latest/_modules/ciscoisesdk/api/v3_1_patch_1/endpoint_certificate.html) creates certificates and is excluded from read-only collection. Guest Location, SMS Providers, and Sponsor Group Members try detail GET operations when Full detail is selected. Availability varies by ISE release. If a detail request returns HTTP 405, the TA retains list summaries with `ise_detail_status=unavailable-http-405`, reports partial coverage, and avoids repeating that detail request for each row during the same poll. The next poll probes detail again. This does not prove that the controller's detail API works; compare the installed ISE API documentation and service-account permissions before treating the warning as resolved. Other HTTP errors remain failures. * **ISE version negotiation:** When the Open API version route is absent, the Monitoring REST fallback requests XML while preserving JSON headers for subsequent Open API collection. Monitoring authorization can still prevent version discovery. * **Advisory completeness:** A sunset Catalyst Center API without a reliable completeness contract remains `recovering` even when observed UI/API counts match. A fresh event or green freshness indicator does not prove a complete snapshot; review the poll's `status`, `output_complete`, and `completeness_proven` fields together. ##### Account setup and permissions * **Monitoring overviews:** New Catalyst Center and ISE sections explain how API context and syslog complement each other, link to permissions and configuration procedures, and include validation and sizing guidance. Catalyst Center's own audit export is distinguished from independent device syslog. SC4S guidance separates local syslog collection from downstream HEC balancing instead of prescribing one global receiver. Both dashboard app links are included without implying that installing dashboards configures collection. * **Product-specific prerequisites:** Account forms link directly to the permission and setup instructions for Catalyst Center, SD-WAN, ISE, and Cyber Vision. The Catalyst Center documentation reference lets you select the Administrator Guide for your installed release instead of pointing only to 2.3.7.x. ISE Analytics Reports has a separate CLI/SSH and repository procedure. A successful authentication test does not prove access to every input; validate the first poll for each enabled input. * **Guest User authorization:** Optional encrypted **Guest REST Sponsor Username/Password** fields allow a separate identity for Guest User reads. Other ERS resources retain the primary identity. HTTP 401/403 remains a failure and identifies the required Guest REST permission; the TA never retries with another identity after rejection. * **Correct ISE account fields:** Monitoring REST credentials appear only on ISE Administrative accounts, not Catalyst Center accounts. Unchanged stored-password placeholders are omitted when saving edits so the existing credentials are preserved. * **Explicit certificate choice:** New REST accounts start with **Verify SSL Certificate** unchecked. HTTPS without certificate verification does not authenticate the server; enable verification for production and supply a trusted custom CA when needed. Saved choices and legacy inherited settings are preserved. SSH host-key checks, Data Connect TCPS, and TLS syslog are unaffected. * **TA-only release:** Companion App and NetFlow Add-on versions remain separate. Earlier collector behavior, sourcetypes, checkpoints, and scale qualification boundaries are unchanged by this account update. ##### ISE Data Connect input registration * **Create and edit coverage:** Application Setup now exposes **ISE Data Connect (Advanced)** and defaults new inputs to `NETWORK_DEVICES`. The same packaged read-only catalogue drives runtime enforcement and the UI options, including views also owned by the domain profiles. Do not select the same view in an advanced input and an enabled domain profile, because both inputs would index it. * **Account test coverage:** **Test Connection** now checks one bounded Data Connect login when its host and password are configured, separates fixed `dataconnect` from the REST user, and performs no view query. * **Guided Data Connect trust:** The ISE account procedure now identifies the version-specific certificate to export, the exact PEM content to paste, and the collector-host TLS checks to use. The TA verifies the configured chain and never automatically trusts a certificate presented by the endpoint. * **Fault-isolated ISE collection:** A failed Data Connect view, ERS resource, Monitoring REST dataset, or pxGrid service no longer prevents later independent configured surfaces from running. Poll diagnostics identify the failed surface and a bounded safe error code; output, transport, deadline, and safety-limit failures still stop the poll. * **Portable `ENDPOINTS_DATA`:** The default projection excludes binary/compressed `PROBE_DATA` and converts `CREATE_TIME` and `UPDATE_TIME` from named-zone timestamps to stable text, avoiding data types unsupported by the portable thin-driver event path. Explicit column overrides cannot re-enable the omitted probe column and retain the timestamp conversion. * **Upgrade-safe advanced inputs:** Existing standalone ERS, Monitoring REST, and pxGrid stanzas remain editable but hidden from the new-input picker. A registry-to-form contract test now fails when a registered product endpoint lacks create or edit coverage. * **Scale boundary:** Each selected Data Connect view is a complete snapshot. Start at 3600 seconds, measure rows and bytes on the largest cluster, and keep p95 poll duration below 80% of the interval before shortening it. ##### Catalyst Center collector completeness * **Client short-page continuation:** When Client page metadata advertises more rows, a nonempty short page no longer ends collection. The next request advances by the number of rows returned, retaining the same time window and stable sort. Older responses without count metadata keep their existing behavior. The heartbeat records `short_pages_continued`; `empty-page-before-count` and `count-not-reconciled` identify incomplete termination. Count drift, duplicate identities, deadlines, and record/byte/page limits remain enforced. This improves coverage but does not guarantee a consistent snapshot from a changing controller list; validate complete polls on the target before comparing UI counts. * **Paginated application catalog:** Application Traffic follows bounded 500-row offset/limit pages, rejects repeated or duplicate pages, and reports page and completeness metrics instead of remaining `recovering` whenever the first page is full. The existing input still represents the application-policy catalog; adding per-interval AVC metrics is a separate data-contract decision. * **Actionable report failures:** Catalyst Center Reports preserves bounded report-name and error-class pairs in its summary and poll heartbeat when one selected report fails, while continuing the remaining selected reports. ##### Data Collection Health coverage * **Automatic product-family discovery:** The dashboard continues to use bounded product namespace searches, so a new `cisco:dnac:*`, `cisco:cybervision:*`, `cisco:sdwan:*`, or `cisco:ise:*` sourcetype appears without another per-panel allowlist. * **One freshness contract:** `cisco_health_set_expected_interval` now owns the expected cadence used by all Data Collection Health freshness searches after legacy names are canonicalized. A new input needs one explicit entry only when its cadence differs from the product-family fallback. * **Complete operator reference:** Catalyst Center Site Health and the current SD-WAN Security Advisory and Insecure Configuration families are included in the source catalog and in-product Sourcetypes Reference. * **Resizable status drill-downs:** Product status tables use wider responsive dialogs, keep compact status and time fields on one line, and provide mouse- and keyboard-operable column resize handles. Constrained screens retain horizontal scrolling instead of compressing diagnostic fields into unreadable columns. * **TA error diagnostic dialogs:** TA Internal Logs tables lead with Severity, Collectors, and Collector Count so operators see urgency and ownership first. Severity and Message cells in the Overview and product-specific tables open a keyboard-accessible dialog. Recognized timeout, authentication, authorization, missing-route, throttling, TLS, connectivity, remote-service, response-contract, and duplicate-ownership patterns receive cautious guidance; unrecognized messages retain a contextual fallback. The dialog preserves the complete raw entry and opens a time-bounded Search scoped to the selected log source, collector host, and severity. * **Device Health site hierarchy enrichment:** The Device Health input can reuse the bounded Site Topology snapshot to populate consistent geographic and typed hierarchy fields. It performs one topology walk per poll, preserves the raw path, reports complete/partial/unavailable enrichment status in poll diagnostics, and leaves fields blank when Catalyst Center does not identify the level. * **Device Health enrichment setting:** Connected **Enrich Site Hierarchy Fields** to the shared input save/edit mapping so enabled and disabled choices are submitted and restored when editing. New inputs retain the enabled default; upgraded inputs inherit the enabled default unless explicitly disabled. * **Version/build evidence on every TA log line:** The shared logger adds the locally installed `ta_version` and `ta_build` to legacy/free-form messages while leaving canonical structured fields unchanged. Upgrade comparisons can therefore use all TA-owned internal logs instead of only `event=` records. ##### Carried-forward collection safeguards * **Optional Stream checks:** Missing packages remain actionable without expected 404/500 errors; Find opens the Splunk-supported Stream search. * **SD-WAN syslog:** Relay monitors default to `cisco_sdwan` with backlog and rotation warnings and need no Splunk restart when created. * **Requirements-first NetFlow setup:** **Protocol-aware NetFlow completion** requires index confirmation and a canary. * **Input setup:** Fresh ISE/Cyber Vision logs use `splunktaciscoise:log`/`splunktaciscocybervision:log`; legacy mappings and retained indexed sourcetypes remain. * **Catalyst Center correctness:** Device Health `cisco:dnac:devicehealth` accepts 750 multi-observation rows/500 devices (`totalCount=1,511`); overlap/deadlines publish partial `recovering` rows. Retries one repeat; inventory drift ≤2 stays partial if UUID counts are bracketed; otherwise fail closed. Defaults: Device Health 900s, Client 3600s, Issue 1,800 seconds. Issues use `firstOccurredTime`, three-row overlap, continuation offsets; 3,944-to-3,939 drift stays partial. A 30,000-issue/24-hour snapshot exceeds one poll. Bounds: 50,000 rows; 17,989 rows require 818 pages below 50 requests/minute. * **Bounded Catalyst Center DEBUG:** Large success JSON becomes SHA-256 metadata; errors retain redacted head-and-tail previews. Customer hostnames, queries, and auth/cookie values are hidden; DEBUG-off avoids parsing; the 99,999-byte cap remains. * **Exact Issue time:** Valid `IssueSpecificTimestamp` sets `seconds.mmm`; payload and `TIMESTAMP_FIELDS` fallback remain. Missing/malformed values never drop events. * **SD-WAN Security Advisories:** Joins Manager snapshots by `icProblemId`; unmatched device references are counted in poll diagnostics, not indexed as complete current advisories. * **Automatic Audit Logs recovery:** The input accepts stable scroll tokens while unique records advance, rejects filter-insensitive POST data, replays affected v4 schema-v2 checkpoints under contract v5, and preserves `cisco:sdwan:audit:logs`; no new audit input or sourcetype. * **Bounded Real-Time recovery:** Malformed HTTP-200 JSON responses are retried within the existing three-attempt limit; terminal failures report bounded content-type/response-size evidence; explicit HTML fails immediately. * **Corrective logging:** Exceptions retain one physical log record; long input URIs remain exact; SD-WAN avoids `NoneType.status_code`; Reports lists emit one canonical `api-error` plus the poll heartbeat. * **Live qualification boundary:** Advisory fixtures cover two APIs; live parity still needs the user-controlled restart and first-poll/index check.

Release Notes:
Changes since v4.0.0. The App and TA release independently: App v4.0.20 requires TA v4.0.50 or later. This entry describes source changes, not publication or production qualification. ##### Dashboards and usability * **Search correctness:** Corrected logical operators in Overview client-health and Security Insights firewall searches. Removed the Performance dashboard dependency on an unavailable ThousandEyes account-group lookup; groups display their IDs. * **Multi-Manager Change Audit:** Added friendly Manager/input labels and exact source isolation across all searches, event details and configuration comparisons. Submitted and deep-linked filters remain authoritative; All Time trends use adaptive buckets. * **Readiness diagnostics:** Added a direct link to the strict-versus-retained diagnostic search. Extra retained summaries appear as collapsed informational compatibility details instead of a not-ready warning. * **Talker and sensor analysis:** Restored Top 10 Talkers drilldowns and added a keyboard-operable Talker details selector. Temperature and humidity charts rank at most ten sensors by peak absolute deviation from each sensor's selected-window average. * **Charts:** All line charts connect across missing values. Optical power and temperature charts are full-width, offer interface and Rx/Tx filters, and plot at most ten series while retaining matching power violations in a summary table. Hidden host filters initialize correctly, and click-time helper fields no longer appear as series. * **Tables and actions:** Master Endpoint Record displays up to 1,000 rows per page with scrolling. Studio tables have more canvas space and readable column widths; Open in Search and visualization actions remain available. * **Status colors:** Restored door-status and Meraki Policy Sync series colors, URL reputation and endpoint completeness table colors, and compliance-card/table colors. Zero failures are green, positive failures are red, and skipped, unavailable or unrecognized requirement states are amber. Severity cards use colored values on white backgrounds. * **Maps and navigation:** Corrected Overview coordinate bindings and added public-IP geolocation fallback. Private addresses require configured ISE location coordinates. Renamed the experimental home dashboard to Overview Beta, distinguished Performance Insights from Cisco IOS Performance, and standardized Implementation Metrics labels. * **Lookup maintenance:** The asset reaper keeps endpoints with valid, non-expired ISE last-seen timestamps and rewrites the KV lookup to remove expired records. Scheduled lookup jobs retain a single `rows_written` summary after writing, while the reaper retains its purge metric. The summary counts submitted rows; it does not independently verify write success or final lookup size. ##### Compatibility, security and packaging * **TA requirement:** Package dependencies and Overview readiness require Cisco Enterprise Networking Add-on v4.0.50 or later. Older, missing or malformed TA versions fail readiness. * **Retained-data compatibility:** Catalyst Center client health, compliance, Device Health, Issue, network health, Security Advisory and Client datasets use TA-owned transition eventtypes. ISE FullReport, Hardware and Registry datasets and asset builders also cover both current and historical report sourcetypes. The App does not duplicate the TA eventtype definitions. * **Dataset constraints:** Added validated constraints for ISE System Health, Syslog Analytics Reports and Application Access, and Cyber Vision Device Vulnerability Events. These retain supported analytics and nested vulnerability records. * **Dependency updates:** Updated brace-expansion, fast-uri, js-yaml, Moment, colord and qs for reported advisories. Current advisory and release qualification checks remain separate. * **Package cleanup:** Excluded 16 replaced Simple XML dashboards while retaining their Studio replacements and repository reference originals. Archives include version and build in `cisco-catalyst-app--.tgz`, with validation against packaged metadata. ##### Upgrade actions 1. Install TA v4.0.50 or later on the collecting tier and search head, then upgrade the App to v4.0.20. Review customer local eventtype overrides if readiness reports an unavailable definition. 2. Hard-refresh open dashboard and editor tabs after upgrading. 3. Retained acceleration summaries remain usable with `allow_old_summaries=true`. Use a controlled rebuild only when transition-eventtype or specialized-dataset constraints must apply retroactively to retained historical buckets. 4. Validate the longest required time range, selected Manager isolation, table pagination, lookup inventory and scheduled jobs in a representative deployment before publication. Bounded plots and submitted-row counts do not establish fleet capacity or lookup completeness.

Description:

Release Notes:
The three dashboards were rebuilt to the approved design: new panels, the brand palette, and a per-engine swarm drawing on Overview and Triage. Two changes are behaviour rather than appearance and matter before you upgrade. **Triage is now a per-indicator detail page.** The free-text base search box is gone; run `polyswarmsearch` in the ordinary search bar over your own search, then open Triage on one indicator from that result's field menu, through the new Triage in PolySwarm workflow action on a hash field. The hash field, indicator limit and time range inputs went with the box. **`polyswarmusage` gained a `refresh` option**, so the Overview entitlement panel reads the stored answer instead of showing an unrendered panel on a fresh install, and reaches PolySwarm only when you select Refresh now. A search that enriches nothing no longer needs a stored credential. Opening any page in the app now costs nothing under any circumstances: the only panel on any dashboard that can reach PolySwarm is Overview's entitlement refresh, and it does so only when you select Refresh now. No role, permission or capability changed, and every search a 1.0.0 install runs today runs the same way. Two smaller things to know on upgrade. **The page background files were renamed.** Splunk serves them with a one year cache at an address that carries no version, so an upgrading install would otherwise have kept 1.0.0's artwork for up to a year; the names now change whenever the artwork does, and your browser fetches the new art on first open. **Four readings came off the Overview entitlement panels**, the plan name, the trial flag, the overage and the plan period, because ten columns in that space left each one narrower than its own sort control. All four are still returned by the searches behind those panels, so `polyswarmusage` in the search bar still reports every one of them. Two panels were also corrected after the first render against a populated cache: the engine swarm's centre now reports the detection count PolySwarm published rather than recounting it from the assertions, so it agrees with the Verdict panel beside it, and the artifact origins chart draws one bar per country instead of plotting country names on a numeric scale.


Short Description:

Description:
The PolySwarm App integrates crowd-sourced malware threat intelligence into Splunk by enriching indicators of compromise with verdicts derived from multiple detection engines. The app processes hashes, URLs, and domains found in Splunk events, annotating them with threat scores, verdict classifications, and detection counts sourced from the PolySwarm platform. It extracts and refangs indicators from raw text fields within the search head environment and submits artifacts to a cloud-based sandbox for behavioral analysis. Search results are augmented with metadata including malware family attribution, file type classification, and aggregated security vendor assessments. The app operates entirely on the search head tier and relies on a key-value store to cache verdict data, track sandbox task state, and maintain modular input checkpoints. Data enrichment occurs through five specialized search commands that query the PolySwarm API, returning threat intelligence without requiring data to leave the Splunk deployment. Events tagged with the polyswarm:artifact source type represent intelligence pulled from the PolySwarm feed and sandbox task results. The app includes dashboards for reviewing enrichment activity, monitoring sandbox detonations, and triaging indicators flagged by scheduled searches. Workflow actions provide analysts with one-click enrichment from search result tables and direct navigation to the PolySwarm portal for detailed artifact analysis.

Users who can search the cluster can still obtain it; minted tokens, per-user credentials and impersonation prevent that * Security: Trace-level logging no longer writes credentials to the search log * Values with commas must be quoted in search commands, for example `labels="app=web,tier=frontend"`, and a parameter given twice is refused * API server certificates with SHA-1 signatures or RSA keys shorter than 2048 bits are refused * Bug fix: `| k8slogs` fails the whole search when one container's logs cannot be read * Bug fix: `| k8sevents` and `| k8sdescribe` report the wrong count and times for events created through the `events.k8s.io` API * Bug fix: On Kubernetes 1.27 to 1.29, `| k8s` cannot find some kinds, such as hpa, pdb, and custom resources * Bug fix: The Networking & Storage claim panels are empty for users who cannot list PersistentVolumes * Bug fix: Some pods and endpoints are counted with the wrong readiness * Bug fix: Dashboards show no value instead of 0 on a healthy cluster * Bug fix: The Setup page does not work for a role with only `edit_k8s_search_clusters`, or next to OS AI Agent or Search for AWS on the same search head


Short Description:
Query your Kubernetes clusters live from the Splunk search bar - like kubectl, as SPL. List resources, stream pod logs, read events, and describe objects across every registered cluster. Read-only and RBAC-controlled. No in-cluster agent, no ingestion, no index storage. Free tier for one cluster; a paid license unlocks multi-cluster and per-user access.


Description:
Kubernetes Search brings live, read-only access to the Kubernetes API into the Splunk search bar. Instead of switching to a terminal and kubectl, you run SPL - | k8s kind=pods namespace=payments - and Splunk queries the cluster's API server directly and streams the current state into your search. The problem it solves: when something breaks in a cluster, the question is usually "what is true right now?" - is the pod still crash-looping, what do its events say, is the node Ready. Answering that has meant leaving Splunk, holding cluster credentials, and running kubectl by hand. Ingestion pipelines give you history, but at the cost of storage and license volume, and they show the cluster only as of the last sample. Kubernetes Search answers the live question from inside Splunk, with no credentials handed out and every query recorded in the Splunk audit log. How it works: - Five search commands cover the common kubectl verbs: | k8s (list or get any resource), | k8slogs (stream pod logs), | k8sevents (cluster events), | k8sdescribe (an object plus its events), and | k8syaml (format JSON as YAML). - Everything runs on the search head and is strictly read-only - it never applies, scales, or deletes anything. - Nothing is indexed: no storage cost, no license volume, no source types, no field extractions. Results exist only for the life of your search. - Register many clusters and fan out with context=* - each row carries a cluster field, so you query and aggregate across your whole fleet from one pane. - Access is gated by a Splunk capability and a per-cluster credential model (shared, per-user, or Kubernetes impersonation), so analysts get controlled, audited read access without being handed kubectl or cluster credentials. - A short-lived on-disk cache keeps dashboards from hammering your API servers; Secrets are never cached. There is no agent to install in your cluster - only a network route from the search head to the API server and a credential. The app installs on search heads only and writes nothing to any index. It pairs naturally with ingestion: use Monitoring Kubernetes or OpenTelemetry for history and trends, and Kubernetes Search for the live picture - in the same Splunk session. Kubernetes Search runs on a free tier with no license key (one cluster, single standalone search head). A paid license unlocks multiple clusters, search head clustering, per-user credentials, and impersonation. Built and supported by Outcold Solutions. Description:
OS AI Agent is an AI assistant that runs inside Splunk, with the model you choose. Point it at the provider you already pay for, or at a model on your own hardware, and ask in plain English: it explores your indexes, writes and verifies SPL, shows every search it ran, and answers with the numbers. Bring your own model. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Groq, and local servers such as LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM or llama.cpp), Anthropic, Azure OpenAI and AWS Bedrock, with retries, failover between providers, prompt caching and Splunk's proxy settings. A local model on your laptop costs nothing per question. It builds, with your approval. Ask for a Dashboard Studio dashboard, a report or an alert. In Chat, anything that writes pauses on an approval card that shows exactly what will be created; approve it, deny it with a reason, or edit it first. It investigates when you are not watching. The "Ask OS AI Agent" alert action and the `| osai` command run read-only investigations from alerts and scheduled searches, and can record a decision, from answers you define, as an event your next alert can act on. **It knows your deployment.** It reads your macros, lookups, data models and installed commands as the signed-in user, follows your query templates and situational guidance, and uses the add-on commands an administrator allows, such as Kubernetes Search or Search for AWS, for data that is in no index. It runs as you. Every tool runs with the calling user's own Splunk permissions, provider keys stay in Splunk's credential store, and an activity trail records every turn, tool call, refusal and configuration change. Token Usage, Activity Trail and Health dashboards show cost per user and provider, what the agent did, and how it is running. Spend limits and a concurrency cap keep a budget a budget. Free to start. Pony Poll — Live Quiz for Splunk turns any Splunk instance into a live interactive quiz — no external database, no middleware, no extra infrastructure. Hosts run timed, scored sessions in two modes: synchronized, where the presenter controls pace and everyone sees the same question at the same second, or self-paced, where each participant moves independently.
